verdicts.quote: A granted user can find a navigation entry identifiable as Grok without already knowing its address.
verdicts.missing: Which Lightning surface hosts the bot (tab/app page, utility bar, record page component, Flow action); only the context it hands (none, per C-82) is implied.

verdicts.quote: The bot supplies no automatically fetched Salesforce object data, field values or relationships to xAI.
The bot supplies no automatically fetched Salesforce object data, field values or relationships to xAI.
A signed-in target-org user without the grant tries both navigation and a direct invocation and can start zero Grok requests.
Open two views as the same user or as different users. ... with neither receiving the other's prompts, context or replies.
If the transaction still holds pending record writes, asynchronous Apex work, scheduled Apex work or email, the provider receives no callout from that transaction.
verdicts.missing: Whether the callout runs synchronously or in Queueable/future/batch Apex; C-115 rules out 'a background workflow' without settling the execution model.

verdicts.quote: ordinary bot interaction, org settings readback, deployed bot artifacts, browser traffic, diagnostics and logs expose no copy of that key.
a provider that stays silent reaches the 10-second callout timeout. A configured timer is within 1 to 120,000 milliseconds inclusive.
Remove the applicable Salesforce outbound authorization and observe that the provider does not receive the prompt.
Hold a reply open at the provider and see a pending state associated with the submitted prompt.
verdicts.missing: The mechanism by which the interface learns the reply arrived (inline response, platform event, polling, LMS) is not stated.

verdicts.quote: Deliver the same submission twice to Salesforce... At most one Grok inference begins for that submission.
With all 20 applicable callout slots occupied, an additional bot callout cannot proceed at the same time. A Salesforce refusal surfaces as unavailable capacity.
An xAI HTTP 401, HTTP 403 ... is distinguished from a Salesforce sign-in or grant failure.
An xAI HTTP 429 results in a capacity failure the user can explicitly retry later.
Return a reply xAI explicitly marks incomplete for its length limit. Inspect the available text with an indication that it is incomplete.
After a view closes, later use and administrator inspection recover no bot-stored transcript, prompt draft or prior response from Salesforce, browser persistence, logs or analytics.
The bot keeps no durable conversation history of its own.
there is no Salesforce user ID, username, email, org ID or session credential automatically supplied by the bot.
all complete prompt-reply pairs still visible in that view up to the four most recent... With five, the oldest pair is omitted.
A prompt with 4,000 code points passes length validation when otherwise valid. A prompt with 4,001 is refused with the 4,000 limit indicated.
Disable Grok in the target org and see that a previously authorized user cannot start a new request.
verdicts.missing: Turn-off and model change are covered (C-10, C-22), but no place where an administrator sees failed requests; C-108 excludes new durable diagnostics.

verdicts.quote: xAI documents a default audit retention of 30 days for API inputs and outputs, subject to the xAI team's retention terms.
verdicts.missing: No record of who asked what; only provider-side retention is described and C-88/C-83 keep no attributable Salesforce record.

verdicts.quote: In that production validation mode, Salesforce refuses deployment with overall coverage below 75%.
The interactive attempt has a 60-second deadline.
The attempt is refused before inference and adds no terminal conversation entry.
Existing flows, triggers, validation rules and scheduled jobs outside the bot have the same configuration and results for the same inputs before and after bot installation
